title: Welp - Cya guys.
author: ajdare
selftext:
I've been moderated and apparently it doesn't matter that you seem to like what I've been posting. Rules are rules. So, starting a new ai game dev community @ aigamerdevs. And I won't mind if anyone shares their creations (commercial or otherwise) gotta support the devs (imho). Cheers and no shade on the mods here - to each their own - just an update for those who have been following my posts and where to find updates now.

https://preview.redd.it/8d30rheug98h1.png?width=606&format=png&auto=webp&s=721401d70a70d902dd371d1dda1092f3ad119dca

comments.author: forrestwear
comments.body: you won't be missed. you post a product/tools (fair), but never respond to criticism. a commenter said they paid for your product, and half the features did not work. no response from you to clarify or anything. even if you're a real person, with real dreams, working hard-- the customer is always right. can't get behind ANYONE selling a product meant to help people, and you can't even guarantee it works. it's just psuedo ads.

replies.author: bloodwolftico
replies.body:
While I do agree sellers should make sure their products work and provide good customer service, the phrase “the customer is always right” has been taken out of context for way too long, and has become a mantra for unreasonable demands.

The full quote is “the customer is always right in matters of taste”, attributed to retail seller Harry Gordon in London in the early 1900s. What this means is that if a buyer wants to buy a horrible shirt you dont stop them or judge them.

But i do agree w the first part of your post about taking criticism and making sure features work.

replies.author: forrestwear
replies.body: ''the customer is always right'' reflects supply and demand. no matter the context of the customer and their demands, it's up to the supplier to meet them IF success is their goal in ANY market. customers are just consumers. naturally you'll have egregious edge cases, but it's up to each person on how they handle and plan for those cases.

replies.author: Lemonface
replies.body:
That's not what "the customer is always right" means. It's a business motto about customer service, not supply and demand. Basically it's better to defer to the customer and take small hits on individual transactions here and there, rather than gain a bad reputation overall as a business 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_customer_is_always_right

replies.author: Lemonface
replies.body:
That's actually an internet myth. The second half was added on about a hundred years later. The full original quote was just "the customer is always right" and it wasn't meant to be limited to customer tastes 

> In the 21st century, social media users and TikTok videos began claiming that the phrase had been abbreviated from "The customer is always right, in matters of taste", with some directly attributing this longer quotation specifically to Selfridge. Fact-checking website Snopes found no evidence for this.

https://www.snopes.com/articles/468815/customer-is-always-right-origin/

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_customer_is_always_right

replies.author: bloodwolftico
replies.body: I see that, you are right. It was popularized by Harry Gordon and others but the 2nd part was added much later.
